name: Kingdom of Laos
native: ອານາຈັກລາວ (Anachak Lao)

predecessors.name: French Indochina
predecessors.text: Laos, 'finally established a sovereign, independent Laos' by the Franco-Lao Treaty of 22 October 1953

successors.name: Lao People's Democratic Republic
successors.text: the whole of Laos, taken by the Pathet Lao: Vientiane on 23 August 1975, the Lao People's Democratic Republic proclaimed on 2 December 1975

successors.name: Pathet Lao
successors.text: Phongsali and Houaphan, held by the Pathet Lao since 1953

ledger.x: 1953: the Kingdom of Laos becomes independent (22 October).
1953: the north-east is in rebel hands from the start.
1957: the Pathet Lao enters the government.
1959: the civil war begins: two Pathet Lao battalions escape integration; 'On 28 July, PAVN units attacked all along the North Vietnamese-Lao border'.
1967: the Ho Chi Minh Trail strip leaves the Kingdom's shape in Cliopatria.
1970: PAVN and the Pathet Lao seize Attapeu (1 May): 'PAVN units (28th and 24A regiments) joined the NVA and Pathet Lao to seize Attapeu'.
1975: the monarchy ends and the Pathet Lao rules the whole country (2 December).
1975: the Plain of Jars passes to the Pathet Lao with the rest of the country (2 December).
1975: the strip ends as Vietnamese-occupied land when the Pathet Lao takes the state (2 December); the Pathet Lao and Hanoi remained allied.
1975: Attapeu passes to the Pathet Lao state (2 December).
1975: the Bolaven Plateau passes to the Pathet Lao state (2 December).
1975: the Kingdom ends (2 December): 'It survived until 2 December 1975'.

wars.name: Laotian Civil War
wars.outcome: Pathet Lao and North Vietnamese victory: the Kingdom of Laos ended and the Lao People's Democratic Republic was proclaimed on 2 December 1975.

certainty.note: Colonial-era frontiers inherited from French Indochina; Phongsali and Houaphan were held by the Pathet Lao without a recorded line.
The Plain of Jars changed hands from 1961 to 1972 and the south-eastern strip was held by PAVN without a recorded line.
